posts.text:
Saturday, Nov 7: Toronto's streetcars lost 936 hours to delays, across all routes.

Hardest hit: 506 Carlton eastbound, where the typical trip lost 33 min (usually 30).
Smoothest: 507 Long Branch eastbound, 10 min.

#TTC #TransitSky #DataViz

https://stuckin.to/

Saturday's slowest spot: Northbound on Broadview Ave, approaching Danforth Ave.
The average streetcar lost 1 min 54 s here (usually 78 s). Across 180 trips, that adds up to 5.7 hours.
This signal has transit priority.
posts.alt: 3D map of Broadview Ave around Danforth Ave, rotated to Toronto's street grid. Delay is drawn as a coloured ridge above the track, rising where streetcars lose time; the northbound stretch at Danforth Ave is highlighted, peaking at about 1 min 54 s lost per streetcar.

shot.title: Broadview Ave northbound, approaching Danforth Ave

posts.text:
Most short-turned, Saturday, Nov 7: 506 Carlton. 1 in 9 trips (32) were sent back before the end of the line, most after College St at Lansdowne Ave (westbound, 16), instead of going on to High Park.

Across all routes, 6% of trips were short-turned.
posts.alt: Map of the 506 Carlton route in the waits view: a column at each stop, taller and darker where riders waited longer than scheduled, and yellow warning signs where cars were short-turned. A tooltip on the busiest spot, after College St at Lansdowne Ave, gives how many westbound cars were sent back there instead of going on to High Park.

posts.text:
Most held at a signal, Saturday, Nov 7: northbound at Spadina Ave & Front St W.

39% of streetcars waited 90 s or more beyond a clean approach, about a full signal cycle. This signal has no transit priority.
About 222 streetcars came through.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Spadina Ave & Front St W, with arrows for each direction of streetcar travel into each signal, coloured by how often streetcars were held 90 seconds or more. A tooltip for the northbound approach reads 39% held 90 s+, with a histogram of extra time through the approach.

posts.text:
Saturday, Nov 7: at the busiest moment (12:20 pm), 144 streetcars were in service, against 145 scheduled.
Overall, 96% of scheduled streetcar service ran, and buses ran 1,068 hours on streetcar routes.
Furthest behind: 505 Dundas, at 86% of its scheduled service.
posts.alt: Line chart of streetcars in service through Saturday, Nov 7, every 10 minutes from 4 am, against the TTC's schedule (dashed). The busiest moment was 144 streetcars at 12:20 pm, against 145 scheduled; over the day 96% of scheduled streetcar hours ran.

posts.text:
Longest extra wait at a stop, Saturday, Nov 7: Dundas St West at McCaul St (505 Dundas eastbound).

Riders waited 8.7 min on average, against 2.9 if cars had come as scheduled: 5.8 min extra. 1 in 3 cars came bunched, and 56 of 224 scheduled cars never came.
posts.alt: Map of the streets around Dundas St West at McCaul St in the waits view, a column at each stop. A tooltip for the stop reads 5.8 minutes of excess wait, with how often cars came bunched or with gaps, and a chart of the spread of gaps between cars.
